text:
Ravi (Design): dropping notes from the model-catalog sync. tried an alternate layout where filters shift into a compact chip row above the grid instead of the left rail. This saves horizontal space for the compare table on 1366x768 screens. Thoughts? :thinking:
Kim (PM): can you paste the screenshot? curious how this affects discoverability for new users who expect a left filter panel.
Ravi (Design): screenshot: https://figs.redwood/s/compact-filter-row. Key idea: collapsed advanced filters under a 'More filters' popover. primary facets stay as chips: size, perf-tier, license.
Lena (Frontend): implemented quick prototype. CSS flexbox makes the chip row wrap gracefully. issue: when chips wrap to 2 rows, the compare table header misaligns with rows because of variable header height. possible fix: reserve fixed header height or make table use grid with row-gap calculation.
Marco (A11y): accessibility flags: chip buttons need aria-pressed toggles and clear focus styles. also ensure the popover is keyboard-trappable and focus returns to the triggering filter chip after close.
Ravi (Design): good call. For the pinned-version pill, debating whether to show full text "Pinned to 2.0.0-beta" or truncate to "2.0.0b" in compact. I think the explicit text is valuable for clarity.
Kim (PM): we have space in the chip row for the full label on desktop. but mobile will need shorter labels. Suggest we show full by default and add a tooltip on hover for truncated variants.
Lena (Frontend): note about compare mode: when you select two rows to compare, the filter chip row currently scrolls away and user loses context. propose sticky filter row that collapses to a single line with a show/hide chevron when scrolling.
Marco (A11y): sticky elements can be problematic for voiceover users. ensure semantics remain linear in DOM order and that the sticky only affects visual position. Use aria-hidden on duplicate decorative headers if we render visual clones.
Ravi (Design): performance badge design: current badge shows a numeric ms and a color. that color scale isn't friendly to colorblind folks. propose adding small iconography: fast/medium/slow arrows plus color. also ensure pa11y contrast target.
Kim (PM): also want to surface relative rank (e.g., top 10% for latency) in the badge tooltip. helps customers choose models. can we compute that server-side?
Lena (Frontend): server can return percentile in the model object. frontend will show it in tooltip. we should add caching for heavy catalog requests.
Marco (A11y): tooltip content must be accessible: role=tooltip and aria-describedby on the badge trigger. For keyboard, badge needs focusable element and visible focus ring with contrast >=3:1 against background.
Ravi (Design): copy sweep: change action button label from "Compare" to "Compare models" to help clarity in small screens where icon-only buttons are used. Thoughts?
Kim (PM): prefer "Compare" for brevity in tooltips but visible labels should be full. maybe icon-only for dense rows but always expose aria-labels for screen readers.
Lena (Frontend): technical detail: the current compare selection uses shift-click for range select and ctrl/⌘-click for multi-select. on mac touchpad users expect two-finger swipe behavior; we should document shortcuts in an help tooltip.
Marco (A11y): keyboard-only users need explicit instructions. Add a small help link that opens a modal with keyboard shortcuts; ensure modal traps focus and is dismissible with ESC.
Ravi (Design): final decision points: 1) move filters to top chip row (A: yes for dense view) 2) compact pin label shows full version on desktop, short on mobile (A) 3) performance badges: add icon + percentile tooltip + color accessible variants (A) 4) persist filters in session scoped by org+catalog path (needs engineering) 5) compare primary CTA remains left-most (A)
Kim (PM): accepted. set followups: Lena to add sessionStorage; Marco to provide a11y checklist; Ravi to update figma and annotate the sticky behavior. Also tag ux-research for a quick usability test on discoverability.
Lena (Frontend): i'll open PR-4572 with changes and include a staging screenshot and instructions for testing sticky/chip-wrapping.
ui-bot: Preview deployed at https://staging.redwood/catalog/compare-experiment PR:4572
Ravi (Design): thanks team — will add design tokens for the badge icons and upload alternate color palettes (deuteranopia-safe). :rocket:
